_meta.source: Illustrative revenue decomposition. Based on NREL ATB cost, energy value from arbitrage, capacity value from ISO resource adequacy (PJM/CAISO/NYISO), ancillary services.
_meta.description: Storage technology economics. Each tech shows: annual arbitrage revenue ($/kW/yr), capacity-market revenue, ancillary service revenue, total value, LCOE, and margin vs LCOE.

technologies.notes: 4hr duration suitable for daily arbitrage; capacity value lower than 8h due to shorter duration.
8hr duration captures both daily and multi-day arbitrage; strong capacity value.
High capital cost. Deep-cycle advantage not yet in value stack (reserve/reliability not monetized). Entry ~2032 at lower CAPEX.
High capex but very long duration and low cycling cost. Limited geographic availability (few remaining sites).

arbitrage.definition: Revenue from buying low-cost hours and selling high-cost hours.
arbitrage.driver: Price spread × round-trip efficiency × power capacity.
arbitrage.example: At 2% daily price delta, 90% RTE, 100 MW: ~$45/kW/yr for 4h duration.

capacity_value.definition: Payment for availability during peak demand hours (ELCC × capacity market price).
capacity_value.driver: Duration × ELCC (empirical or RPM/CONE-based) × capacity price ($/kW-yr).
capacity_value.notes: ERCOT is energy-only; other ISOs pay via capacity markets. Longer duration → higher ELCC.

ancillary_services.definition: Revenue from regulation, reserves, and voltage support.
ancillary_services.notes: Often absorbed by larger generators; standalone battery value lower than full fleet.

forecast_trajectory.notes: Learning curve: ~10% CAPEX decline per year (Wright's Law). Margins improve with cost decline + higher power prices.
